_schema.purpose: Inventory of chemical species injected into the upper atmosphere by the space industry, across both pathways (satellite reentry ablation and launch exhaust). Consumed by Multi-species-accumulation.py.
_schema.reading_this_file: Every quantitative field carries a `status`. Do not use a value whose status is `unquantified` or `speculative` as though it were measured. The point of this file is to make the difference visible, not to fill every cell.

status_values.sourced: Value taken from a named external publication. See `reference`.
status_values.repo_assumption: Value chosen inside this repo. Traceable to a model file, not to a measurement.
status_values.unquantified: Known to be present, but this repo has no flux estimate for it.
status_values.speculative: A guess, present only to make a mechanism expressible. Never cite.

coupling_mechanism_values.em_conductivity: Alters stratospheric/mesospheric electrical conductivity — the mechanism this project's chi coefficient is about.
coupling_mechanism_values.radiative: Scatters or absorbs radiation; direct radiative forcing.

_schema.verification_warning: The `reference` fields below were gathered via web search on 2026-08-14. Direct access to the publisher PDFs was blocked by this environment's network egress policy, so abstracts and secondary summaries were the sources, NOT the full papers. Every one is marked `verified_against_primary: false`. Check them against the primary source before citing. See RESEARCH_LOG.md U-14.

murphy2023.citation: Murphy, D. M., et al. (2023). Metals from spacecraft reentry in stratospheric aerosol particles. PNAS, 120(43), e2313374120.
key_findings_as_retrieved: Over 20 elements from reentry detected in stratospheric aerosol, in ratios consistent with spacecraft alloys.
Niobium and hafnium do not occur as free elements in nature and are refined from ores, making them distinctive spacecraft tracers.
About 10% of stratospheric sulfuric acid particles larger than 120 nm contain aluminium and other spacecraft-reentry elements.
The reentry mass of lithium, aluminium, copper and lead exceeds the cosmic dust influx of those same metals.
Projection: planned LEO constellation growth could raise the affected fraction to roughly 50%, comparable to the fraction now containing meteoric metals.

ferreira2024.citation: Ferreira, J. P., et al. (2024). Potential Ozone Depletion From Satellite Demise During Atmospheric Reentry in the Era of Mega-Constellations. Geophysical Research Letters, 51.
key_findings_as_retrieved: A typical 250 kg satellite generates approximately 30 kg of aluminium oxide nanoparticles on demise.
Al2O3 from the entire 2022 reentry population estimated at approximately 17 metric tons.
A realised mega-constellation scenario reaches over 360 metric tons per year.
Reentry byproducts may take up to 30 years to settle from the top of the mesosphere into the stratospheric ozone layer.
Mechanism: aluminium oxides do not react with ozone directly. They trigger chlorine activation, and are not consumed, so a single particle can destroy ozone repeatedly for decades.

rocket_emissions_survey.citation: Multiple: Maloney et al. (2022) JGR Atmospheres 10.1029/2021JD036373; Ryan et al. (2022) Earth's Future 10.1029/2021EF002612; rocket-emitted chlorine study, ACP 26, 3621 (2026).
key_findings_as_retrieved: Solid rocket motors burn aluminium fuel with an ammonium perchlorate oxidiser, emitting hydrochloric acid and alumina particles.
Alumina particles act as reaction surfaces for chlorine, accelerating ozone loss.
Launch emission inventories cover chlorine, NOx, H2O, CO2, black carbon and alumina.
A 10x increase in rocket chlorine emissions over 2019 gives near-global column ozone loss below 0.1 DU (0.04%); a 52x increase gives 0.6 DU (0.23%).

species.name: Aluminium oxide (reentry)
species.origin_component: Satellite structural airframe, oxidised during mesospheric ablation
species.projected_injection_note: Mega-constellation scenario, per ferreira2024. Not a present-day rate.
species.residence_time_note: Time to settle from the top of the mesosphere into the stratospheric ozone layer. This repo implements it as a rectangular kernel — full retention then instant removal — which is not what a settling time means. See U-3.
species.catalytic_ozone_note: Indirect. Does not react with O3; activates chlorine and is not consumed. Therefore CO-LIMITED BY AVAILABLE CHLORINE — see hcl_launch and RESEARCH_LOG H-12.
species.em_coupling_weight_note: Reference species, weight fixed at 1.0 by definition. This is the only species the chi model has ever used.

species.name: Lithium
species.abundance_note: Reentry mass exceeds the cosmic dust influx of lithium (murphy2023). That is a floor on significance, not a flux figure.
species.em_coupling_weight_note: Lithium is highly electropositive and readily ionised, so a conductivity contribution is physically plausible. Plausible is not measured. No value is supplied.

species.name: Copper
species.abundance_note: Reentry mass exceeds the cosmic dust influx of copper (murphy2023).
species.em_coupling_weight_note: Bulk copper is the reference high-conductivity metal, which makes it the most tempting species to assign a large weight. Resist that: bulk conductivity does not transfer to a dispersed oxidised nanoparticle aerosol. Unresolved — see U-12.

species.name: Lead
species.abundance_note: Reentry mass exceeds the cosmic dust influx of lead (murphy2023).
species.toxicity_note: The only species here with a well-established human-health regulatory framework. That framework governs surface air, not the stratosphere, so it does not currently apply.

species.name: Niobium
species.tracer_note: Does not occur as a free element in nature; only reaches the stratosphere refined. Presence is therefore unambiguous evidence of spacecraft origin — no meteoric confound (murphy2023). This is the attribution key for the whole inventory.

species.name: Hafnium
species.tracer_note: As with niobium: not naturally free, so unambiguous spacecraft attribution (murphy2023).

species.name: Remaining reentry elements (aggregate)
species.aggregate_note: murphy2023 reports over 20 elements from reentry detected in stratospheric aerosol, in ratios consistent with spacecraft alloys. Six are named individually above. The remainder are real and detected but are not itemised in this inventory, because the sources available to this repo did not enumerate them. Candidates by alloy composition — titanium, iron, chromium, nickel, silver, zinc, magnesium, beryllium — are INFERENCES FROM MATERIALS, not detections reported here. Do not present them as observed. See U-11.

species.name: Alumina (launch exhaust)
species.origin_component: Solid rocket motors — aluminium fuel with ammonium perchlorate oxidiser
species.pathway_note: Chemically identical to the reentry product, deposited by a completely separate pathway that this repo does not model at all. Any 'total atmospheric Al2O3 burden' computed from reentry alone is an UNDERCOUNT by whatever this pathway contributes. Magnitude unknown. See H-11.
species.em_coupling_weight_note: Same species as the reference, so same weight. Note this does NOT mean the two pathways deposit at the same altitude or particle size — they may not, and that would matter.

species.name: Hydrogen chloride / reactive chlorine
species.origin_component: Ammonium perchlorate oxidiser in solid rocket motors
species.criticality_note: The most consequential omission in this repo. Al2O3's ozone effect runs THROUGH chlorine activation (ferreira2024) — alumina supplies the reaction surface, chlorine does the destroying. So satellite reentry and rocket launches are not two independent problems: the reentry pathway's ozone impact is co-limited by a launch-pathway species. Neither is modelled jointly here. See H-12.
species.sensitivity_as_retrieved: 10x increase in rocket chlorine over 2019 gives <0.1 DU (0.04%) near-global column ozone loss; 52x gives 0.6 DU (0.23%). Note these are small compared with this repo's headline ozone claims — a tension worth resolving rather than ignoring. See U-13.

species.name: Black carbon / soot
species.origin_component: Hydrocarbon propellants (kerolox and most others); minor from reentry ablation of composites
species.radiative_note: Strongly absorbing, and deposited directly in the stratosphere where it is not rained out. Per the retrieved sources this is a leading climate term for launch emissions — a mechanism entirely absent from this repo, which models conductivity and ozone but not direct radiative forcing.
species.em_coupling_weight_note: Elemental carbon is electrically conductive, so an em_conductivity pathway is arguable. Not established. No value supplied.

species.name: Nitrogen oxides
species.origin_component: Shock-layer heating during both launch ascent and reentry; fixes atmospheric N2
species.note: Classical NOx catalytic ozone loss, independent of the chlorine and alumina pathways. Appears in the launch emission inventories cited. Generated on BOTH pathways, since both involve hypersonic shock heating of air.

species.name: Water vapour
species.note: Stratospheric water vapour is radiatively active and supports polar stratospheric cloud formation, which in turn enables heterogeneous chlorine chemistry. Another route by which a 'clean' propellant is not inert at altitude.

species.name: Sulfur dioxide (stratospheric aerosol injection)
species.origin_component: Proposed solar geoengineering, not a space-industry emission
species.note: Included because this repo's README and executive summary both invoke Al/S catalytic synergism as a central claim. Listed here so that claim has somewhere to attach. NOT AN OBSERVED FLUX — SAI is a proposal, not a deployed programme. The synergism claim itself has no supporting run anywhere in this repo. See U-15.
